title: Hosted API sentinel connection leak — P0 streaming + 503 wave postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2027-11-29 02:08 UTC we observed a global spike in streaming request 5xx responses and sustained tail-latency increases for the Hosted API. Impact lasted ~3h with intermittent recovery windows. Root cause traced to a gradual leak in the multiplexer "sentinel" bookkeeping (connection reference counters not being decremented under a specific error path), which allowed ephemeral streaming connections to accumulate on edge mux nodes. That accumulation caused acceptor thread starvation, queueing of RPCs to downstream model backends, increased KV-cache prefetch latency, and ultimately request timeouts and 503s for streaming sessions.

Why this is notable (short):
- Failure surface: edge multiplexer -> acceptor queue blowup -> downstream prefetch/backpressure -> streaming timeouts and 5xx cascade.
- Triggered by an uncommon error combination (TLS renegotiate during client disconnect + code path introduced in recent multiplex refactor).
- Early symptoms were subtle (slow rise in in_flight connections metric) before large visible impact.

Impact:
- 2.8% of streaming requests returned 5xx or aborted during the main window (02:08–05:25 UTC).
- Regional variability: US-West and Europe had highest incidence due to route affinity to particular edge rings.
- Some mission-critical customers experienced degraded UX (chat stalls, reconnect loops).
- No data loss; requests were failing fast in the gateway layer.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:04 — alert: streaming_error_rate > baseline (auto-alert fired).
- 02:08 — on-call SRE triaged and saw growing acceptor.queue_depth on mux-edge-prod-7.
- 02:12 — initial mitigation: enabled temporary routing-policer to divert new streaming sessions to non-multiplexed path for affected rings. Latency briefly improved but error rate persisted.
- 02:25 — discovered abnormal climb in multiplex.in_flight_connections metric; sessions not closing as expected.
- 02:40 — memory and descriptor counts on mux-edge-prod-7 trending up; suspected leak.
- 03:05 — rollback of multiplex refactor flag (toggled to previous behavior) on two control-plane cells; acceptor queue depth began to decline.
- 03:45 — applied conservative acceptor backpressure (lower max_inflight_per_node) cluster-wide to limit further accumulation while we prepared patch.
- 04:20 — hotfix PR merged and rolled to edge mux golang binary: explicit sentinel decrement on TLS-renegotiate error path and stronger finalizers in connection manager.
- 05:08 — rollout complete; global metrics returned to baseline by 05:25.

Root cause analysis (why):
- Code change: a multiplex refactor (merged 2027-11-20) introduced a change in the sentinel lifecycle: a rare error path that occurs when a client triggers TLS renegotiation was missing the sentinel-decrement call.
- That missing decrement meant the in-memory counter on the edge mux never reached zero for many short-lived streaming sessions; GC/finalizers were slow to reclaim because connections were still referenced in a small ring buffer.
- The slow accumulation was amplified by synthetic traffic patterns from a large customer (high short-lived stream churn) which exposed the leak quickly.
- The acceptor queue is sized to absorb transient spikes; persistent accumulation pushed queueing into long-tail latencies and backend prefetch timeouts (KV-cache prefetches blocked on slow acceptor processing).

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Diverted new streaming sessions away from affected multiplex rings to non-multiplexed path (reduced new accumulation).
- Rolled back multiplex refactor flag on 2 control-plane cells responsible for the most traffic.
- Globally reduced max_inflight_per_node for acceptor to limit per-node accumulation.
- Emergency hotfix to sentinel lifecycle: added missing decrement, defensive nil-checks, and added metrics for sentinel_acquire / sentinel_release mismatch counts.

Longer-term fixes and follow-ups (action items):
1) Code/Runtime fixes (owner: Marco Alvarez) — due 2027-12-10:
   - Land and GA the sentinel lifecycle hotfix with full unit + fuzz tests for rare TLS error paths.
   - Add systematic test harness simulating high churn short-lived streams + TLS renegotiation scenarios.

2) Observability (owner: Zoe Kim) — due 2027-12-03:
   - Create sentinel_acquire vs sentinel_release mismatch alert (SLO-aware) and dashboard tile.
   - Add an alert for sustained positive slope in multiplex.in_flight_connections over 5m with region breakout.
   - Add acceptor.queue_depth heatmap to ops console showing top offending nodes.

3) Runbook updates (owner: Ravi Desai) — due 2027-12-06:
   - Add explicit triage steps for suspected mux connection leak: metrics to check, quick mitigation toggles, and validated rollback play.
   - Document safe thresholds for max_inflight_per_node scaling and rollback instructions.

4) Traffic engineering (owner: Tina O'Neil) — due 2027-12-08:
   - Add temporary routing guard to detect rings with > 15% short-lived stream churn and shift new sessions to fallback pool automatically.

5) Post-release verification (owner: Aisha Patel) — due 2027-12-01:
   - Run a 48h canary with churned synthetic traffic across multiplex and non-multiplexed paths.

Runbook (draft) — triage checklist for mux leak suspicion:
- Step 1: Check multiplex.in_flight_connections (region + ring). Look for steady upward trend > 5% over 5m.
- Step 2: Check acceptor.queue_depth and acceptor.thread_utilization on affected nodes.
- Step 3: If in_flight connections growing and queue depth > threshold, enable routing diversion to non-multiplexed fallback for the ring.
- Step 4: If diversion reduces new in_flight growth, rollback recent multiplex-related flags or toggle to previous behavior.
- Step 5: If immediate fix not available, apply conservative max_inflight_per_node reduction cluster-wide and contact code owner.
- Step 6: After mitigation, run sanity traffic and monitor sentinel_acquire/release mismatch metric.

Monitoring/Dashboards to add (short list):
- sentinel_acquire_count, sentinel_release_count, sentinel_mismatch_count (per ring).
- multiplex.in_flight_connections (5m derivative, per region).
- acceptor.queue_depth (p50/p95/p99) with node-level drilldown.
- kvcache.prefetch_latency and prefetch_timeouts (to catch downstream knock-on).

Lessons learned / notes to self:
- Subtle resource bookkeeping bugs can evade standard unit tests — we need targeted chaos tests for edge cases (TLS renegotiate + churn).
- Routing fallbacks are valuable but must be exercised regularly via chaos or drills so engineers are familiar with side-effects.
- Alerts should be slope-aware (detect growth) in addition to absolute thresholds for connection/resource metrics.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why were GC/finalizers not reclaiming references fast enough? Follow-up between runtime infra and Go team to understand timing tradeoffs (linked ticket SRE-9126).
- Should we accept occasional short-lived mismatch spikes during high churn? Need to set safe operational thresholds.

Appendix — quick pointers used during incident (commands & queries):
- kql: sum by(ring) (increase(multiplex_in_flight_connections_total[5m]))
- kql: topk(10, acceptor_queue_depth{env="prod"})
- log query: "sentinel acquire" | "missing release" | parse_error:tls_renegotiate

Postmortem action summary (owner assignments repeated):
- Marco Alvarez — code hotfix + test harness — due 2027-12-10.
- Zoe Kim — dashboards & alerting — due 2027-12-03.
- Ravi Desai — runbook + playbook docs — due 2027-12-06.
- Tina O'Neil — routing guard policy — due 2027-12-08.
- Aisha Patel — canary coordination + post-release verification — due 2027-12-01.

Status: in_review. Uploading this draft to SRE channel for comments before marking final.

Notes: a few informal callouts from on-call log:

- "03:12 — traffic diversion gave a 60% immediate drop in new 5xx but old sessions still flapped until patch applied"
